Report_ID: Smoking abstinence (7-day point-prevalence, ITT) at 6 months
Title: Motivation and patch treatment for HIV+ smokers: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Lloyd-Richardson et al.
Comment: Paper reports only percentages, not raw quitter counts; group_1_events/group_2_events left empty rather than back-calculated from rounded percentages (9% of 232 and 10% of 212 would be ~21 each). Randomised Ns used as totals (232 ME, 212 SC).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Motivationally enhanced (ME) counselling + NRT') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Recruitment source: Referrals from six out-patient HIV clinics and two primary care medical offices, southeastern New England
Outcome variable: Smoking abstinence (7-day point-prevalence, ITT) at 6 months
effect_direction: favours control (9% ME vs 10% SC; no significant difference)

Report_ID: Tobacco use cessation: biochemically confirmed 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6 months (ITT)
Title: A randomized trial of a web-based tobacco treatment and online community support for people with HIV attempting to quit smoking cigarettes
Author: Shuter et al.
Comment: Paper reports odds ratios only; no risk ratio named. Event counts over randomised N are provided for downstream RR computation. Control arm is an attention-matched active health website rather than brief advice/no intervention.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('PSFW+ (web-based behavioural cessation intervention with online community) + offer of 12 weeks nicotine patch') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults with HIV who currently smoke cigarettes and are motivated to quit
Recruitment source: Two urban HIV care clinics (Bronx NY; Baltimore MD) via provider referral, clinic waiting areas, flyers
Outcome measurement: Self-reported no cigarette in past 7 days verified by ECO<10ppm (salivary cotinine where ECO≥10ppm)
Outcome variable: Tobacco use cessation: biochemically confirmed 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6 months (ITT)

Report_ID: Smoking cessation: 7-day point prevalence abstinence at 3 months
Title: Efficacy of Cell Phone–Delivered Smoking Cessation Counseling for Persons Living With HIV/AIDS: 3-Month Outcomes
Author: Vidrine, Marks, Arduino, & Gritz
Comment: Paper reports odds ratios only (age-adjusted logistic regression); no risk ratio is reported, but raw ITT event counts and denominators are given and recorded so RR can be computed downstream. p value reported as "<.0001" and entered as 0.0001. Both arms received brief advice + self-help + NRT instructions (NRT not systematically provided), so this maps to the 'behavioural support alone vs brief advice' subgroup.
Topic of Content: Cognitive-behavioural smoking cessation counselling (problem solving, skills training, relapse prevention)
Participant type: Adults living with HIV/AIDS who smoke (>=5 cigarettes/day)
Recruitment source: Thomas Street Health Center HIV care clinic, Houston, Texas
Outcome measurement: Number of quitters / number randomised per arm (ITT)
Outcome variable: Smoking cessation: 7-day point prevalence abstinence at 3 months

Report_ID: Smoking abstinence (CO-verified 7-day point prevalence) at 52 weeks — Individual counseling + NRT vs Self-help (brief) + NRT
Title: A Randomized Clinical Trial of Smoking Cessation Treatments Provided in HIV Clinical Care Settings
Author: Humfleet, Hall, Delucchi, & Dilley
Comment: The paper does NOT report raw quitter counts or per-arm denominators in text; Figure 1 (participant flow) is an unreadable image. Event counts/totals were reconstructed as the unique small-integer fit to the reported week-52 percentages (Counseling 20.41% = 10/49; Brief 19.72% = 14/71). The shared self-help control arm (14/71) was then split approximately in half across the two behavioural-support variants per the shared-control-splitting instruction (this row: 7/36; CBI row: 7/35, summing to 14/71). Denominators correspond to participants assessed at week 52, not to the number randomised. The odds ratio is adjusted (mixed-effects nonlinear regression including completer status, employment, desire to quit, POMS mood disturbance, usual cigarettes/day, assessment week) and is for the condition main effect across all assessments, not week 52 alone. M_diff holds the model estimate (0.20, log-odds coefficient) for the Counseling term.
Participant type: HIV-positive adult smokers recruited from three HIV clinics
Recruitment source: University of California San Francisco AIDS Health Project, Positive Health Practice at San Francisco General Hospital, Tenderloin Health
Outcome measurement: Percent abstinent per treatment condition at week 52; model-based odds ratio for Counseling condition
Outcome variable: Smoking abstinence (CO-verified 7-day point prevalence) at 52 weeks — Individual counseling + NRT vs Self-help (brief) + NRT
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: Computer-based Internet treatment (CBI) + NRT, 25.58% abstinent at week 52 (extracted as a separate row, E2)
effect_direction: favours intervention marginally (20.41% counselling vs 19.72% brief self-help; not significant)

Report_ID: Tobacco use cessation: 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6 months (ITT)
Title: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of Intensive Group Therapy for Tobacco Treatment in HIV-Infected Cigarette Smokers
Author: Stanton et al.
Comment: Table 2 lists P = 0.94 for this same 6-month comparison while the Results text states P = 1.0; the text value was recorded. No risk ratio is reported by the paper (OR only); event counts preserved for RR computation downstream.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('PSF intensive group therapy + offer of 12-week nicotine patch supply (behavioural support + NRT)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Persons living with HIV who currently smoke cigarettes and are motivated to quit
Recruitment source: HIV-care centers in the Bronx, New York and Washington, DC (provider referral, clinic waiting-room invitation, self-referral to fliers)
Outcome measurement: Number of quitters out of number randomised per arm
Outcome variable: Tobacco use cessation: 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 6 months (ITT)
effect_direction: favours control marginally (13.0% vs 13.3%, OR 0.97; no difference)

Title: Smartphone App and Carbon Monoxide Self-Monitoring Support for Smoking Cessation: A Randomized Controlled Trial Nested into the Swiss HIV Cohort Study
Author: Gryaznov, Chammartin, Stoeckle, Anagnostopoulos, Braun, Furrer, Boillat-Blanco, Bernasconi, Schmid, Nordmann, Bucher
Comment: Paper reports only an adjusted odds ratio (adjusted for past quit history, baseline cigarettes, and prescribed NRT/withdrawal drugs); no risk ratio is reported, so RR must be computed downstream from the extracted event counts (6/42 vs 5/39). Trial terminated prematurely (81 of 496 planned) and is underpowered. 3 participants lost to follow-up were counted as smokers.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention: CO self-monitoring with mobile phone-based feedback + Stop-tabac.ch app in addition to standard smoking cessation care (behavioural support)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Medium: mobile phone app + CO monitoring device + text messages
Participant type: HIV-positive adults in the Swiss HIV Cohort Study smoking ≥3 cigarettes per day
Recruitment source: Swiss HIV Cohort Study biannual cohort visits at Swiss HIV centres
Outcome measurement: Number of quitters out of number randomised per arm
effect_direction: favours intervention marginally (14% vs 13%, aOR 1.06; no difference)

Report_ID: 7-day point prevalence smoking abstinence (CO-verified) at 12 weeks
Title: Combining Text Messaging and Telephone Counseling to Increase Varenicline Adherence and Smoking Abstinence Among Cigarette Smokers Living with HIV: A Randomized Controlled Study
Author: Tseng, Krebs, Schoenthaler, Wong, Sherman, Gonzalez, Urbina, Cleland, Shelley
Comment: Shared-control splitting applied per synthesis plan: the single SC arm (3/53 abstinent) is divided equally between the two behavioural-support variants, giving 1.5/26.5 for this row (raw, unsplit values are 3/53). Odds ratio 5.51 is from the adjusted GLMM (covariates: time, adherence, baseline heaviness of smoking, independent housing), not an unadjusted 2x2 statistic; the Table 2 p = .07 is a 3-arm Fisher's exact test, while p = .05 is the SC+TM+ABT vs SC model contrast.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('SC+TM+ABT (varenicline + text messaging + 7 telephone adherence-focused motivational/behavioral therapy sessions)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adult cigarette smokers living with HIV (>=5 cigarettes/day, willing to quit within 2 weeks)
Recruitment source: Waiting areas of three HIV care centers affiliated with St. Luke's-Roosevelt Hospital Spencer Cox Centers for Health, New York City
Outcome measurement: Number abstinent / number randomised per arm at week 12
Outcome variable: 7-day point prevalence smoking abstinence (CO-verified) at 12 weeks
additional_group_ns: SC+TM arm (varenicline + text messaging only), n = 54, 2/54 (3.7%) abstinent at week 12 — extracted as its own separate row
